summary: Space Machine Case Files is a free browser detective game for kids aged 8–12. Each machine NASA left on the Moon and Mars becomes a cold case: kids watch a briefing, search a dark crime scene with a flashlight, study evidence built from real NASA data, and accuse the culprit (the Dust, the Cold, the Sand Trap and more). A wrong guess gets an alibi that sends them back to the evidence. Each solved case shows the lesson that lived on and a five-minute experiment to try at home. For the “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, it turns NASA hardware that was left behind into stories kids solve themselves, so they remember the machines and the science behind them.
details:
What it does: seven playable cases (Opportunity, Spirit, Phoenix, InSight’s mole, Ingenuity, the Apollo 17 Moon buggy and the Apollo laser mirrors) with six villains, 36 evidence cards, 34 cited sources and seven home experiments.

How it works: every case has five steps. (1) A briefing shown as security-camera footage with real mission dates. (2) A flashlight search of a pixel-art crime scene. (3) An evidence room with interactive cards: a dust slider that dims the Martian sky to the real record of tau 10.8, Phoenix before-and-after orbit photos, Ingenuity’s navigation camera, and a laser you fire at the Moon to time the real 2.56-second round trip. (4) A suspect lineup, where wrong answers return alibis. (5) Case closed: the truth, a twist, the lesson that lived on, and a home experiment. A notebook collects every experiment and source for parents and teachers.

Why it matters: kids learn that engineers learn from failure, and they practise reasoning from evidence instead of memorising facts. It runs on any phone or laptop with no install or login. Text types itself live, and a crime-scene soundtrack is generated in the browser. It includes tap-to-skip, a no-sound mode and reduced motion.

Goals: a Hindi version, a teacher mode linked to the school syllabus, two more Moon cases (Surveyor 3 and the descent stages), and a pilot with schools in Lucknow.

Built with: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single web page, Canvas for the pixel art, and the Web Audio API for live sound. The demo video was made with Playwright, Python and ffmpeg.
